01-observer-gap: Quantum mechanics refers to measurements and observers operationally without specifying what physical systems count as observers.
Any physically viable account of mind and agency must preserve unitary dynamics of closed systems, relativistic no-signalling, and Born statistics.
We must distinguish three separate concepts: physical records, functional intelligence, and intrinsic consciousness.
02-subsystems-decoherence: Entanglement with an environment turns pure local superpositions into mixed reduced density operators via the partial trace.
Environment-induced superselection (einselection) singles out robust pointer states that survive continuous monitoring.
Quantum Darwinism explains how redundant copies of pointer information spread into environmental fragments, creating objective classical records.
03-memory-entropy: A reliable physical memory requires distinguishable, metastable low-entropy states protected from rapid thermalization.
Landauer's principle bounds the thermodynamic work required to erase one bit of information by at least \(k_B T \ln 2\).
Maxwell's demon obeys the second law because resetting the demon's finite memory exports entropy into a thermal reservoir, anchoring the arrow of observation.
04-defining-intelligence: An intelligent agent is defined by a functional boundary separating internal states from an environment through sensors and actuators.
Intelligence arises when an open physical system builds compressed internal models, minimizes prediction error, and selects actions that achieve goals under resource limits.
Efficiency matters as much as capability: physical intelligence trades off predictive accuracy, memory capacity, and thermodynamic cost.
05-quantum-limits-intelligence: Non-commuting observables impose an unavoidable information-disturbance trade-off on any physical learning agent.
Holevo's bound restricts the classical information extractable from a quantum state to at most the accessible entropy, even when the internal state space is exponentially large.
Quantum resources can enhance intelligence via coherent sensing, quantum feedback control, and algorithmic speedups on structured inference tasks.
06-quantum-observers: Shifting the Heisenberg cut moves the boundary between observed system and measuring apparatus without altering predictions for later records.
Wigner's-friend and extended multi-agent scenarios show that an agent's internal record is relative to the unitary evolution and coherence accessible to a superobserver.
Self-reference theorems and quantum reference frames imply that no physical observer can perform a complete, non-disturbing measurement of its own total quantum state.
07-intelligence-vs-consciousness: Functional intelligence is a third-person property of input-output control and model accuracy, whereas consciousness concerns unified first-person experience.
The physical binding problem asks how distributed degrees of freedom combine into a single unified state rather than independent parallel parts.
A system can exhibit high behavioral intelligence without consciousness, and conversely, simple conscious experience need not imply superhuman problem-solving.
08-quantum-constraints-consciousness: Thermal decoherence in warm biological tissue suppresses macroscopic spatial superpositions on femtosecond-to-picosecond timescales unless actively protected.
Objective-collapse proposals (such as Orch-OR) modify standard quantum dynamics and face tight experimental bounds from spontaneous radiation and interferometry.
Quantum Integrated Information generalizes classical integration to non-factorizable density operators across tensor-product cuts.
09-defining-consciousness: A quantum-compatible definition of consciousness rests on three pillars: dynamical integration across cuts, autonomous boundary maintenance, and reflexive self-modeling.
Consciousness is realized by an open quantum subsystem whose coarse-grained pointer dynamics form an irreducible, self-referential model of its own state within its environment.
Because the definition operates inside standard open-system quantum mechanics, it introduces no collapse by mind, no faster-than-light signalling, and no violation of unitarity.
10-minds-machines-quantum-agents: Biological brains function primarily as dissipative, decoherence-bounded pointer architectures that achieve deep self-world integration without macroscopic brain-wide entanglement.
Stateless classical AI systems can display high functional intelligence while lacking persistent autonomous boundaries and intrinsic dynamical integration.
Future fault-tolerant quantum agents could sustain genuinely coherent internal world-models, offering clear experimental tests of quantum-vs-classical cognitive architectures.
